sources.title: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - The Drunk Beaver XR Series MD-1 Medal Mind is a superb take on the Exar MD-03 and MD-04 - originally inspired by the Boss MT-2 Metal Zone
sources.h1: The Drunk Beaver XR Series MD-1 Medal Mind is a superb take on the Exar MD-03 and MD-04 - originally inspired by the Boss MT-2 Metal Zone
sources.excerpt: Sep 9, 2026 08:00 by Stefan Karlsson Distortion Drunk Beaver Drunk Beaver XR Series Metal Distortion + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points The Drunk Beaver XR MD-1 Metal Mind reworks the Exar MD-03/MD-04 and Boss MT-2 Metal Zone dual-gain-stage architecture with low-noise op-amps, power supply filtering, true-bypass switching, fixed filters, and active three-band EQ. Controls include Gyrator Lows (86Hz), Mids (533Hz), High-Pass Filter (7.2kHz), Level, and Metal/Gain. Fixed filters are 1063Hz, 4.9kHz, and 102Hz. Preferred settings are Low max, High and Level noon, Metal 3 o’clock, with Mid minimum for Vintage or 3 o’clock for Modern. It costs $90 / €90 / 349 PLN. Pair of Pandas has the only demo so far. A potent take on the dual-gain-stage Boss MT-2 Metal Zone architecture — this MD-1 Metal Mind pedal overhauls that vintage topology with modern low-noise op-amps, robust power supply filtering, true-bypass switching, and an active three-band EQ with fixed midrange voicing. The pedal has an incredibly low noise floor, and significant range on every dial. You’ll often hear me say that a pedal could do with a little more volume or gain - while this one is pretty much spot-on. It’s already plenty loud enough for me at Noon - and I have the other half of that taper still in reserve! Polish locals are well aware of the prowess of the MD-03 and MD-04 Exar Metal Mind pedals - which largely copy the Boss gain architecture - but go with a more straightforward 3-Band Active EQ, rather than the Boss’s 3-Band EQ with semi-Parametric Mids. Lots of players don’t get on with the Boss 2-pot Mids - they find it really fiddly to dial things in properly, and often get frustrated. So instead this pedal has a single-knob Gyrator Mids - which allows for much easier control, and overall more satisfaction for those who struggle with the MT-2 controls. Controls - Active Gyrator Lows [cf 86Hz], Active Gyrator Mids [cf 533Hz], Active High-Pass Filter [cf 7.2khz], Level, Metal / Gain. Essentially the Bass, Mids are Gyrators - peak/bandpass filters, While High is a High-Pass Filter. The pedal also has fixed filters - before the gain stage : 1063Hz bandpass, and post gain stage / before EQ at 4.9kHz, and 102Hz. That is a huge part of how precise this pedal sounds, and how low its noise floor. And as you would imagine - it's incredibly easy to dial in! My Preferred Vintage Settings are - Low @ Max, Mid @ Min, High @ Noon, Level @ Noon, Metal @ 3 o'c. My Preferred Modern Setting are - Low @ Max, Mid @ 3 o'c, High @ Noon, Level @ Nono, Metal @ 3 o'c. Incredibly - as I mentioned earlier - the pedal is already loud enough at noon. 3 o'c is as much as I want to take it on the Gain / Metal side. I pretty much leave Highs at Noon too, while I can Max out the Bass, and the Lower-Mids. But for the Modern setting I don't like to go above 3 o'c - as beyond that it starts to alter the texture of the pedal and add more noise. The XR MD-1 Metal Mind - is a total step at just $90 / €90 / 349 PLN. You can by the few remaining first batch editions direct from the Drunk Beaver Rocks Webstore . Before the locals snap them all up. There will of course be more - and I expect this one to do really well!
